key_findings: Most candidate biomarkers remain insufficiently reliable or clinically actionable; schizophrenia resting-state connectomics remains promising

methods: Multilayer network modeling of resting-state fMRI modularity
key_findings: Schizophrenia showed higher flexibility in cerebellar, subcortical, and frontoparietal systems
limitations: Results sensitive to methodological choices; flexibility not clearly superior to simpler metrics

methods: Resting-state connectome predictive modeling with independent validation
key_findings: Baseline connectome features predicted PANSS improvement in discovery and validation cohorts
limitations: Task-specific predictive biomarkers still need broader external validation

methods: Spatially constrained ICA with rsFNC classification
key_findings: 2-4 minute scans retained diagnostically relevant rsFNC information
limitations: Conference paper and focused on one preprocessing framework

key_findings: LC-TEC pathways were reconstructed reliably and linked to CSF tau
limitations: Specialized pathway focus rather than whole-brain connectome

methods: Tractography-based edge density imaging with validation dataset
key_findings: White matter tracts associated with BMI overlapped with tracts predictive of AD conversion
limitations: Sample relatively modest and focused on obesity-conversion overlap

key_findings: WMH-related tract disconnection mediated executive, memory, and language associations
limitations: Indirect tract mapping rather than native subject tractography

methods: Resting-state fMRI plus diffusion tractography and machine learning
key_findings: Structural anomalies clustered in DMN/subcortical regions while functional anomalies were more heterogeneous
limitations: Preliminary cohort and limited emphasis on generalization

key_findings: Mean edge-wise ICCs were poor (<0.4) despite stronger multivariate reliability
limitations: Depression cohort, not general whole-brain connectome benchmark

methods: Test-retest reliability of principal FC gradient across cohorts
key_findings: Gradient-derived measures were more reliable than edge-wise FC and improved with longer scans
limitations: Gradient summaries may sacrifice some edge-level interpretability
